h1: The 6 Best Garden Carts and Wagons of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six garden carts and wagons, sorted by capacity, flatbed or dump design, tires, material and price tier.
summary: The Gorilla Carts steel utility cart is the best all-round garden cart, with a 1000 lb flatbed in sturdy steel. The Gorilla dump cart is the pick for mulch and soil, and the 900 lb VEVOR is the budget steel wagon. The BILT HARD adds handling for small yards, and the poly Gorilla suits light loads.
intro: Garden cart shoppers sort by pounds, but the first real decision is shape. A flatbed carries long, awkward items such as potted shrubs, lumber and bagged mulch, while a dump cart tips loose material out in one motion. Pick the wrong shape and every job turns into a wrestling match, no matter how high the rating climbs.

We assessed six carts from their spec sheets and owner reports about daily yard work, ranking capacity, bed design, material, tires and price tier. We kept a spread of designs on purpose, so the tradeoffs are visible instead of six near copies. A cart that matches your usual load beats a bigger one every time, so we scored fit for the job alongside raw numbers, and we flagged listings that say little.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Steel Utility Garden Cart, 1000 lb. Capacity, Gray
products.verdict: The highest capacity flatbed here, in sturdy steel.
products.description:
The Gorilla steel utility cart is the cart for people who want one cart. A steel flatbed rated at 1000 lb is the highest-capacity flatbed here, and a flatbed accepts the widest range of loads: potted plants, firewood, tools, bagged soil and the odd paving stone. Steel frames resist the flex that makes cheaper carts feel loose under weight.

It ranks first because versatility beats specialization for most yards. The VEVOR 900 lb wagon costs about half as much but lists little beyond capacity, while the Gorilla dump cart carries more but only suits loose material. At $100 to $200, the steel Gorilla is priced between the two.

Buy it as the cart that does most things. Skip it if you mostly move loose soil, because a flatbed has no dump function and every load must be shoveled or lifted out by hand.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Dump Garden Cart, 7 Cu Ft, 1200 lb Capacity, No-Flat Tires
products.verdict: The highest capacity cart here and the best for tipping loads out.
products.description:
The Gorilla dump cart is the specialist. A 7 cu ft bed, a 1200 lb capacity and no-flat tires make it the strongest cart on paper, and tipping a full load of mulch or leaves is far easier than shoveling it from a flatbed. No-flat tires matter because a cart that lives in a shed too often has a soft tire on the day you need it.

It lands second because a dump bed is less useful for awkward, flat or tall items, which are half of what most yards ask of a cart. It also sits in the $200 to $500 tier, the priciest here, while the flatbed Gorilla above costs a tier less.

Choose it if you move mulch, soil, gravel or leaves regularly. Skip it if you carry long boards or tall pots, because the sloped sides get in the way.

products.name: VEVOR Heavy Duty Steel Garden Cart 900 lbs Garden Wagon Cart on Wheels
products.verdict: A steel wagon rated for 900 lbs at a much lower price.
products.description:
The VEVOR 900 lb steel wagon is the budget heavy hitter. It lists a 900 lb capacity and steel construction in the $50 to $100 tier, which is roughly half the price of the Gorilla steel cart. For general hauling around a yard, that rating covers nearly any load you would put on a wagon.

It ranks third because the brand has less of a track record and the listing says little beyond capacity. You gain price, not documented extras like tire type or bed volume. Against the 500 lb VEVOR below, the 900 lb version is a far better buy at similar money.

It suits budget-minded buyers who want a strong steel wagon for general work. Skip it if you want a dump bed. Expect to check the assembly and bolts, because a cheaper cart can ship with loose fasteners.

products.name: BILT HARD 400 lbs 10" Rubber Tires Steel Garden Cart with 180° Rotating Handle and Removable Sides
products.verdict: A smaller steel cart with a rotating handle and removable sides.
products.description:
The BILT HARD is the cart that handles like one. A 400 lb capacity pairs with 10 inch rubber tires, a 4 cu ft bed, a 180 degree rotating handle and removable sides. The rotating handle lets you pull or push from either end, and the sides come off to make a flatbed for long items.

It ranks fourth because the capacity is lower than the larger carts and the bed is smaller. In exchange, it turns easily in tight spaces and converts between wagon and flatbed. At $50 to $100 it competes directly with the 900 lb VEVOR, which carries more but lacks the flexibility.

Choose it for a small to mid-size yard where flexibility matters more than raw capacity. Skip it for heavy material like wet soil or stone, since 400 lb is a real ceiling when loads are dense. Steel can rust if scratched, so touch up the paint.

products.name: VEVOR Steel Garden Cart 500 lbs Heavy Duty Garden Wagon Cart on Wheels
products.verdict: The lowest priced steel wagon for lighter work.
products.description:
The 500 lb VEVOR is the plain steel wagon. It lists a steel build and wagon design in the $50 to $100 tier, and nothing more. For light jobs such as moving pots and bags, that is enough, and the simple design has less to break.

It ranks fifth because its capacity sits well below the 900 lb version for little savings. Both sit in the same price tier, so the step down in rating buys you almost nothing. The BILT HARD adds handling features and the poly Gorilla adds dumping at similar money.

Buy it if you want a simple steel cart for light work and do not need maximum capacity. Skip it if you ever haul wet soil or stone, because 500 lb disappears quickly. The listing is also thin, so check wheel size and bed dimensions before ordering.
products.idealFor: Light jobs on a tight budget.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Poly Dump Cart, 2-Wheel Garden Wagon, 4 Cu Ft, 300lb Capacity
products.verdict: A light, rust-proof two wheel dump cart for small loads.
products.description:
The poly Gorilla is the light dump cart. A 4 cu ft bed, a 300 lb capacity and two wheels make it small and easy to move, and the poly body resists rust, which steel carts cannot claim. Dumping works the way a wheelbarrow does, tipped forward.

It ranks last because 300 lb is the lowest rating here, and two wheels are less stable than four. The tipping action needs your lifting, which matters with a loaded bed. The BILT HARD is steadier at 400 lb, and the VEVOR wagons carry more for the same $50 to $100 price.

Choose it for frequent, small loads in a small garden, where light weight and rustproof construction matter. Skip it if you carry heavy material or work on uneven ground. Poly can crack in extreme cold, so store it indoors in winter.

whatMatters.detail: A flatbed carries long or awkward items and loads easily, while a dump bed tips out loose material in one move. Pick the one that matches your most common job, because switching later means buying a second cart. Check whether the listing says dump or lists a tilt feature, and measure the bed length against your longest item.

The pound rating is the structural limit, and it matters less as loads get awkward. Dense loads like wet soil weigh much more than they look, and a full bed can overshoot the rating quickly. Compare the rating with your heaviest regular load, then leave a margin so the cart does not live at its limit.

Steel is strong but can rust if scratched, while poly resists rust and is lighter but can crack or fade in the sun. Pick by climate and how rough you are on the cart. Check the listing for the material, and look for powder coat or paint if the cart will sit outside.

No-flat and rubber tires avoid punctures, while air-filled tires ride softer over bumps. For a cart that sits in a shed between jobs, flat-free tires save the trouble of a soft tire on the day you need it. Look at the tire size and type, because bigger wheels roll over roots more easily.

Four wheels are steadier under load, and two wheels turn tighter. A two-wheel cart behaves like a wheelbarrow and needs your lifting to carry the weight. Count the wheels in the listing and check the axle, and consider your yard layout: tight turns favor two wheels, long straight paths favor four. Also check whether the front axle pivots or the handle steers.

faq.q: Do I need a dump or a flatbed cart?
faq.a: Dump for loose material like soil and mulch, flatbed for bags, plants and awkward items. If you do both, the BILT HARD with removable sides is a compromise, though its 400 lb rating limits the heavy jobs.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a cart?
faq.a: Ignoring the design type. A high-capacity dump cart like the Gorilla 1200 lb is awkward for boards and pots, and a flatbed is slow for loose soil. Choose the shape before the rating, then compare capacity within that shape.

faq.q: Is the Gorilla cart worth it over the VEVOR?
faq.a: The Gorilla offers more capacity and a known brand, while the VEVOR 900 lb gives a high rating for roughly half the money. If you want a dump bed, the Gorilla dump cart is the pick.

faq.q: How do I prevent rust on a steel cart?
faq.a: Rinse off soil, dry the bed and touch up scratches with paint before storing under cover. Steel carts like the VEVOR and Gorilla utility cart need this more than the poly Gorilla, which resists rust on its own.

faq.q: How do I assemble a garden cart?
faq.a: Most arrive flat-packed. Set aside an hour, attach the wheels and handle and tighten all bolts, following the manual's order. Recheck the fasteners after the first loaded week, since they can settle.

faq.q: Can I use a garden cart on slopes?
faq.a: Yes with light loads, but a two-wheel cart like the poly Gorilla gives you less control on a grade. The larger carts are heavier when full, so keep loads smaller on slopes and walk beside the handle, not ahead of it.

finalTake: For most yards, the Gorilla steel utility cart is the right garden cart, with a 1000 lb flatbed that handles nearly any job. Choose the Gorilla dump cart for mulch and soil, the VEVOR 900 lb wagon for budget hauling, and the BILT HARD or poly Gorilla when handling and size matter more than capacity.
